title: Lesson 6
paragraph: 仕事の引き継ぎと協力

words.meaning: to contact someone briefly to exchange news or check progress
words.japaneseMeaning: 短く連絡を取り状況を確認する
words.example: Let's touch base on Friday to see how the preparations are going.

words.meaning: to bring an activity or discussion to an end
words.japaneseMeaning: 活動や話し合いを締めくくる
words.example: We should wrap up the meeting before lunch.

words.meaning: to prepare a formal document or detailed plan
words.japaneseMeaning: 正式な文書や計画を作成する
words.example: The lawyer will draw up the agreement this week.

sentencePractice.prompt: The terms have been agreed, but no written contract exists. A lawyer will ____ a contract that records those terms.
sentencePractice.reviewNote: Creating the missing formal document requires drawing it up. Tearing up destroys an existing document; turning down refuses it.

words.meaning: to tell someone an idea in order to hear their opinion
words.japaneseMeaning: 案などを人に話して意見を聞く
words.example: I will run the proposed schedule by Maya before sharing it with the team.

exampleGap.prompt: I will ____ before sharing it with the team.
exampleGap.answer: run the proposed schedule by Maya

words.usageNote: something と someone は内容や人名に置き換えます。例: run the idea by Maya。

words.meaning: to begin controlling something or doing a job that someone else was doing
words.japaneseMeaning: 引き継ぐ、管理を引き受ける
words.example: Who will take over the project when Lina leaves?

words.meaning: to leave an important official position
words.example: The chair plans to step down after ten years.

sentencePractice.prompt: After leading the organization for ten years, she has decided to ____ and let a new chair replace her.
sentencePractice.reviewNote: Allowing a new chair to replace her means leaving her position. Taking over begins leadership; staying on continues it.

words.meaning: to do someone's job temporarily while they are absent
words.japaneseMeaning: ～の代わりを一時的に務める
words.example: Can you fill in for our receptionist on Monday?

words.meaning: to have so much work that it is difficult to manage
words.japaneseMeaning: 仕事に追われて手が回らない
words.example: The accounts team must be snowed under at the end of the year.
words.usageNote: 主に会話で、仕事量の多さを強調する比喩です。be snowed under with work の形も使います。

words.meaning: to make more effort than is normally expected
words.japaneseMeaning: 期待以上の努力をする
words.example: Our guide went the extra mile by finding an accessible route for us.

words.meaning: to stop working on something for the rest of the day
words.japaneseMeaning: その日の仕事を切り上げる
words.example: We have finished the urgent repairs, so let's call it a day.
